solutionSql: SELECT customer_id, id FROM (SELECT customer_id, id, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY booked_at DESC, id DESC) AS rn FROM shipments) ranked WHERE rn = 1 ORDER BY customer_id;

rules.howSolved: row_number() ordered by booked_at DESC keeps the latest booked shipment as row 1 within each customer.
PARTITION BY customer_id makes the ranking, and so the choice, separate for each customer.
The window is computed over shipments only, so a customer with no shipment rows never appears in the output.
The secondary sort key id DESC puts the greater id first when booked_at is equal.

ambiguities: None material. I read 'most recent by booked_at' as the latest timestamptz value; booked_at is NOT NULL in the schema, so no NULL ordering question arises.
notes: Ran with no errors on sample (6 rows), ties (6 rows) and boundary (6 rows). Only row counts were observed for the hidden datasets. solveMinutes is a self-estimate, not a timed measurement. Result objects are keyed by column name in sampleFirstRows.
